questions.text: Why add semantic endpointing to a voice activity detector when deciding whether a user has finished their turn?

options.A: To reconstruct a waveform from the transcript.
options.B: To identify the user from a voice embedding.
options.C: To eliminate the need to capture audio frames.
options.D: To distinguish a pause within a thought from a completed turn.

questions.explanation: VAD detects speech activity; semantic endpointing adds context to judge whether a silent pause means the user is finished.

questions.text: Your streaming recognizer buffers look-ahead audio and explicitly supports flushing. Once turn end is detected, how can you request the remaining transcript promptly?

options.A: Discard buffered audio and transcribe only the next turn.
options.B: Send the remaining audio, issue a flush, and receive the final transcript.
options.C: Increase the silence hangover by the recognizer’s full look-ahead delay.
options.D: Replace the recognizer’s sample rate metadata without resampling.

questions.explanation: A supported flush asks the recognizer to process buffered audio and emit the remaining transcript rather than wait for more audio.

questions.text: In the shown TurnDetector, speech adds 20 to speech_ms; idle silence does not reset speech_ms. Starting idle with min_speech_ms=60, what happens on speech, silence, speech, silence, speech?

options.A: END is emitted on the final chunk.
options.B: No event occurs because speech was never consecutive.
options.C: START is emitted on the final chunk.
options.D: START is emitted on the first chunk.

questions.explanation: The toy code accumulates speech_ms across idle gaps: 20, then 40, then 60. It emits START on the final speech chunk, despite the gaps.
